source_title: Analysis of neurodegenerative disease-causing genes in dementia with Lewy bodies

expected_evidence.value: GRN; APP; CHCHD2; DCTN1; MAPT; NOTCH3; SQSTM1; TBK1; TIA1; GBA; APOE; PLCG2; SNCA; PRNP; SNCB
GRP p.Arg493* is a known pathogenic FTD-causing mutation; identified here in a DLB patient, potentially adding to the diversity of phenotypes associated with this mutation
GRCh37/hg19
c.2020G>A (APP); c.10G>A (CHCHD2); c.2339T>C (DCTN1); c.827C>T (GRN); c.256G>A (MAPT); c.1732C>T (NOTCH3); c.1733G>A (NOTCH3); c.1820G>A (NOTCH3); c.1210A>G (SQSTM1); c.1150C>T (TBK1)

p.Arg493* (GRN); p.Glu674Lys (APP); p.Gly4Arg (CHCHD2); p.Ile780Thr (DCTN1); p.Ala276Val (GRN); p.Gly86Ser (MAPT); p.Arg578Cys (NOTCH3); p.Arg578His (NOTCH3); p.Arg607His (NOTCH3); p.Met404Val (SQSTM1); p.Arg384Trp (TBK1)
nonsense (GRN p.Arg493*); missense (all others)
GRN p.Arg493* is a nonsense (truncating) mutation; previously reported as pathogenic loss-of-function in FTD
GRN p.Arg493* protein truncation; remaining variants are amino acid substitutions of uncertain significance

NOTCH3 p.Arg578His at same residue as CADASIL p.Arg578Cys; NOTCH3 p.Arg607His at same residue as CADASIL p.Arg607Cys; TBK1 p.Arg384Trp at same residue as ALS p.Arg384Thr; APP p.Glu674Lys adjacent to AD-associated p.A673T/p.A673V
GRN p.Arg493* causes premature truncation
Analysis focused on amino acid changing variants and those in splice donor/acceptor sites, splice regions, or 5'/3' UTRs
GRN p.Arg493* predicted null (nonsense/LoF) variant
1004 DLB patients analyzed after QC (from initial 1118)
Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)
Neuropathologically diagnosed DLB per 2005 McKeith guidelines, meeting 'intermediate' or 'high' likelihood criteria

GRN p.Arg493* patient: episodes of confusion, memory loss, disorientation, altered gait, stooped posture, right-sided rigidity, visual hallucinations, impaired smooth pursuit, left hemiparesis, left spasticity, parkinsonian tremor of left hand, severely demented (MMSE 3/30); stroke and prior subdural haematoma in history
GRN patient assessed at 83 years, approximately 2 years before death; cohort mean age at death 78.8 (±8.4) years
Family history of AD with onset in the seventh decade (parent and sibling)
Cohort male to female ratio 1.5
Caucasian / European (clustered with 1000 Genomes European population)
No pathogenic homozygous variants identified in autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disease genes; compound heterozygous variants could not be fully assessed (data not phased)
Whole exome sequencing (Illumina Nextera Rapid Expanded Exome 62 Mb or Agilent SureSelect Exome Capture Kit v4) on Illumina HiSeq2500; candidate variants confirmed by Sanger sequencing

On-target average coverage of at least 30x; GATK v3 best practices, joint variant calling, VQSR threshold 99.9; genotypes with phred quality <20 or coverage <8 set to missing; variants required genotyping in >=90% of samples in both capture kits
432 control individuals from the Healthy Exomes (HEX) dataset who died aged 60 or over without any disease-associated neuropathology
Data not phased; compound heterozygous variants could not be completely assessed
gnomAD v2.1 (125,748 exomes and 15,708 genomes); Healthy Exomes (HEX) dataset (432 controls)

APP p.Glu674Lys: 0 (not present); CHCHD2 p.Gly4Arg: 0.00002840; DCTN1 p.Ile780Thr: 0.00003889; GRN p.Ala276Val: 0.000007075; MAPT p.Gly86Ser: 0.00002901; NOTCH3 p.Arg578Cys: 0.00003989; NOTCH3 p.Arg578His: 0.000007980; NOTCH3 p.Arg607His: 0.000004000; SQSTM1 p.Met404Val: 0.00001591; TBK1 p.Arg384Trp: 0.00002128
APP: not present; CHCHD2: 4; DCTN1: 5; GRN p.Ala276Val: 1; MAPT: 4; NOTCH3 p.Arg578Cys: 2; NOTCH3 p.Arg578His: 0; NOTCH3 p.Arg607His: 1; SQSTM1: 3; TBK1: 4
CHCHD2: 128432; DCTN1: 129150; GRN p.Ala276Val: 129048; MAPT: 126300; NOTCH3 p.Arg578Cys: 113234; NOTCH3 p.Arg578His: 113200; NOTCH3 p.Arg607His: 112826; SQSTM1: 113732; TBK1: 128892
European (non-Finnish) / NFE in gnomAD

Variants of uncertain significance included if present five times or less in the European (non-Finnish) population in gnomAD; previously reported pathogenic mutations were rare in this cohort, suggesting limited genetic overlap of other neurodegenerative diseases with DLB
DCTN1 p.Ile780Thr also found in a control; NOTCH3 p.Arg578Cys also seen in 1 control
Annotation performed with snpEff v4.2 and dbNSFP v2.9
Case cohort exome sequencing study with comparison to population frequency databases (gnomAD) and a neuropathologically normal control dataset (HEX)
1004 DLB cases analyzed (1118 initially)
432 HEX controls; gnomAD v2.1 comprising 125,748 exomes and 15,708 genomes
Patients neuropathologically diagnosed as 'intermediate' or 'high' likelihood DLB per 2005 McKeith guidelines, self-reported Caucasian
HEX controls died aged 60 or over without disease-associated neuropathology; gnomAD used as general population reference

Maximum tolerated allele count estimated using alleleFrequencyApp (cardiodb.org) based on Alzheimer's disease as a conservative approximation; sample QC via PLINK 1.9, PCA for population structure, identity-by-descent threshold >=0.1875 for relatedness
Rarity of previously reported pathogenic mutations suggests genetic overlap of other neurodegenerative diseases with DLB is not substantial
GRN p.Ala276Val was previously reported in a patient whose initial diagnosis of FTD was changed to depression
MAPT p.Gly86Ser segregation not proven; PRNP and SNCB variants previously questioned due to lack of segregation
DCTN1 p.Ile780Thr found in a control; NOTCH3 p.Arg578Cys seen in 1 control; PRNP/SNCB variant pathogenicity questioned due to presence in healthy controls
MAF/population presence and non-segregation noted for several VUS
ClinVar used as one of the sources to identify previously reported pathogenic mutations
Literature search used HGMD, OMIM, AD & FTD and PD mutation databases, and ClinVar to identify previously reported pathogenic mutations
GRN p.Arg493* previously reported pathogenic (FTD); NOTCH3 p.Arg578Cys and p.Arg607Cys known CADASIL pathogenic; SQSTM1 causes Paget's disease of bone; APP p.A673V causes EOAD when homozygous

NOTCH3 p.Arg578His and p.Arg607His are different amino acid changes at the same residues as known pathogenic cysteine-changing CADASIL variants (p.Arg578Cys, p.Arg607Cys); TBK1 p.Arg384Trp differs from ALS-reported p.Arg384Thr at the same residue

variants.null_variant_detail: Nonsense mutation in GRN (ENST00000053867); known FTD-causing loss-of-function variant, confirmed by Sanger sequencing in one patient

variants.protein_effect: APP (ENST00000346798); adjacent amino acid p.A673T protective, p.A673V causes EOAD when homozygous
CHCHD2 (ENST00000395422); previously reported in 1 LBD patient
DCTN1 (ENST00000361874); found in 2 DLB cases; previously in 1 FALS patient and a control
GRN (ENST00000053867); previously reported in a patient whose FTD diagnosis was changed to depression
MAPT (ENST00000344290); previously reported in 1 patient with clinical FTD, segregation not proven
NOTCH3 (ENST00000263388); found in several CADASIL patients but also in 1 control; homozygous carrier had mild phenotype
NOTCH3 (ENST00000263388); different amino acid change than CADASIL p.Arg578Cys, not cysteine-changing
variants.same_amino_acid_known_variant: Same residue 578 as known pathogenic p.Arg578Cys (different amino acid change)

variants.protein_effect: NOTCH3 (ENST00000263388); p.Arg607Cys seen in several CADASIL patients; filtered site in gnomAD, may be false positive, not cysteine-changing
variants.same_amino_acid_known_variant: Same residue 607 as known pathogenic p.Arg607Cys (different amino acid change)

variants.protein_effect: SQSTM1 (ENST00000389805); shown to cause Paget's disease of bone (not FTD-ALS)
TBK1 (ENST00000331710); p.Arg384Thr (different amino acid change) reported in 1 ALS
variants.same_amino_acid_known_variant: Same residue 384 as p.Arg384Thr reported in ALS (different amino acid change)
